prs.title: Fix `token_expiry_time` upon context initialization for stored tokens.
prs.author: keurcien
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Stored OAuth tokens don't survive a restart with correct expiry tracking: OAuthContext.token_expiry_time is never recomputed when tokens are loaded from storage in `_initialize()`, so `is_token_valid()` treats an actually-expired stored token as valid, the proactive-refresh branch in `async_auth_flow` is skipped, and the client falls all the way through to an interactive re-authorization instead of silently refreshing. PR #2875's own inline comment states this exact root cause verbatim. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Stored OAuth tokens don't survive a restart with correct expiry tracking: OAuthContext.token_expiry_time is never recomputed when tokens are loaded from storage in `_initialize()`, so `is_token_valid()` treats an actually-expired stored token as valid, the proactive-refresh branch in `async_auth_flow` is skipped, and the client falls all the way through to an interactive re-authorization instead of silently refreshing. PR #2875's own inline comment states this exact root cause verbatim. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: #1784 fixes the actual root cause with a 4-line change in `_initialize()` that recomputes `token_expiry_time` via `update_token_expiry()` when stored tokens are loaded, and ships a new `expired_tokens` fixture plus test asserting the fix. #2875 doesn't touch `_initialize()` at all; it papers over the same bug by inserting a new 'Step 3.5' refresh-token attempt inside the 401 handler in `async_auth_flow` before falling back to full re-auth. That's a larger, more invasive change to a shared hot path (it now fires an extra token refresh attempt on every 401, not just ones caused by the stale-expiry bug), and once #1784's root-cause fix restores `token_expiry_time` correctly, the existing proactive-refresh branch upstream of the 401 handler already covers this case, making #2875's added branch redundant.

clusters.pick_reason: 3056's `_is_optional_str` narrowly matches only `str | None` (Optional[str]) — the exact shape in the bug report — and its docstring spells out why: no other member of that union could ever result from JSON-decoding a string, so skipping pre-parse there is safe, while pre-parsing is preserved for every other union shape (e.g. `str | int`, `str | list[str]`). 2032's `_should_pre_parse_json` instead skips pre-parsing whenever ALL union members fall in a broader `{str, int, float, bool, NoneType}` set, regardless of whether `str` is even present — so it also disables pre-parsing for unions like `int | bool` or `str | int` that have nothing to do with the reported string-corruption bug, a wider behavior change than the fix requires.

clusters.pick_reason: 3056's `_is_optional_str` narrowly matches only `str | None` (Optional[str]) — the exact shape in the bug report — and its docstring spells out why: no other member of that union could ever result from JSON-decoding a string, so skipping pre-parse there is safe, while pre-parsing is preserved for every other union shape (e.g. `str | int`, `str | list[str]`). 2032's `_should_pre_parse_json` instead skips pre-parsing whenever ALL union members fall in a broader `{str, int, float, bool, NoneType}` set, regardless of whether `str` is even present — so it also disables pre-parsing for unions like `int | bool` or `str | int` that have nothing to do with the reported string-corruption bug, a wider behavior change than the fix requires.
